name: web-stylebook-mcp

tools.name: recommend_design_direction
tools.description: Given product context, return scored style candidates with reason codes, rejected styles with reasons, secondary pairings, assumptions and confidence. Evidence-provider: the host model makes the final pick. Call before writing UI. The "tone" field (named "tone", not "tones") is an ARRAY of zero or more of: calm, technical, trustworthy, premium, editorial, playful, bold, experimental. Each candidate.score already includes adjustments (soft penalties, repeated-use load, closeness to avoided styles) that are not itemized in scoreBreakdown. The "ranking" field says why candidates[0] outranks the next style, or reports a tie; list the most important tone first because tone order is weighted. Each candidate.structure gives the page structure the direction implies: a layout archetype (hero composition, grid, section order, density, type-scale use), 2-3 signature moves with their purpose, and the generic and style-specific patterns audit_page_structure will flag; read structure.resourceUri for move build steps and ban criteria. The top-level mustHaves lists the elements the resolved product type requires (for example price, variant choice, add to cart, and delivery details on a commerce product page) with the zone each must sit in; a style restyles them but never removes them, they come before the archetype's limits on the opening, and each candidate.structure.mustHaves names the signature moves that can present them. Pass the same productType to audit_page_structure to find the ones a built page is missing.

tools.name: compare_design_directions
tools.description: Compare 2-4 directions across product fit, repeated-use suitability, density, trust, distinctiveness, accessibility risk, motion and maintenance. Returns each direction's favorable conditions and likely failure mode — never a single winner.

tools.name: search_design_references
tools.description: Search the bundled, attributed real-world design reference library. Query text is matched deterministically against titles, ids, categories, tags, and localized analysis. category is an exact filter; every supplied tag must match case-insensitively. Returns concise localized observations and resource links, never screenshots or brand assets.

tools.name: get_design_reference
tools.description: Return one complete localized design reference with observed palette, layout, interaction, motion, normalized tokens, source revision, CC BY attribution, adaptation notice, and original-site rights notice. Use it as research evidence; do not copy or redistribute excluded screenshots, brand assets, copy, typefaces, or visual identity.

tools.name: get_design_principle_plan
tools.description: Select a small set of practical visual-design principles for intent and iteration, semantic hierarchy, adaptive layout and density, typography and localization, tokens and themes, accessible interaction, and complete states and recovery. Filter by design concerns, surface, phase, or explicit ids. Returns placement guidance, application steps, verification checks, cautions, related principles, and deterministic relevance scores.

matchMode.description: ranked-union scores any matched selector dimension; all-selectors requires every supplied dimension and may return no matches

tools.name: get_ux_principle_plan
tools.description: Select a small, evidence-labeled set of UX principles for a target outcome, surface, design phase, or explicit principle ids. Returns design questions, application steps, verification checks, cautions, references, and relevance scores. Treat the result as decision prompts rather than universal laws.

matchMode.description: ranked-union scores any matched selector dimension; all-selectors requires every supplied dimension and may return no matches

tools.name: get_design_audit_plan
tools.description: Return a localized, surface-aware audit checklist with stable check ids, severity, applicability, required evidence, remediation, verdict definitions, user-facing content checks, selected principle checks, and UI-state coverage. The host should confirm audit coverage and change depth with the user before choosing includeGroups. Include the opt-in "structure" group (with styleId) to add automated checks for banned generic and style-specific page patterns, answered by audit_page_structure; add productType to that group for one check per product must-have. This tool does not inspect a project: the host must collect actual rendered/code/interaction evidence, and missing evidence is NOT_VERIFIED rather than PASS.

productType.description: with the "structure" group, adds one check per must-have of this product type

tools.name: audit_page_structure
tools.description: Deterministically inspect submitted page markup (offline; the server never reads files) for the generic SaaS template (centered hero over a gradient blob, all-text centered stack, stock-photo hero, logo strip, "trusted by" band, icon feature cards, testimonial carousel, generic closing CTA banner, and the page skeleton they form) and, with styleId, for that style's own banned treatments. With productType, it also reports which of that product type's must-haves (the same list recommend_design_direction returns) the page is missing or keeps off the first screen. Pass the rendered HTML (for example document.documentElement.outerHTML) and the page's CSS text; Tailwind utility classes are understood without the stylesheet. Each finding names the location, the observed values, and what to replace it with from the chosen style's signature moves and archetype. Also returns evidence and results shaped for validate_design_audit_result with the "structure" audit group. Declared-style heuristics, not a browser: a clean result is not a design pass. Limits: html 1500000 characters, 20 stylesheets, 3000000 CSS characters in total.

productType.description: the product type passed to recommend_design_direction; adds its must-have checks

tools.name: validate_design_audit_result
tools.description: Regenerate the requested audit plan, then deterministically validate target coverage, evidence references, required evidence types, verdict applicability, and contradictions. This tool does not inspect artifacts or judge visual quality. It normalizes unsupported PASS/FIX_NOW/RISK claims to NOT_VERIFIED, preserves honest NOT_VERIFIED results, and returns stable plan/evidence/result hashes for comparable rechecks.

productType.description: with the "structure" group, adds one check per must-have of this product type

tools.name: get_ui_state_plan
tools.description: For a surface (data-table, form, checkout, chat, developer-console), return required / recommended / domain-specific states with triggers, must-show, must-not, accessibility and motion guidance, plus an implementation order. Covers the non-happy-path.

surfaceId.description: surface id — one of: data-table | form | checkout | chat | developer-console

styleId.description: optional catalog style id (see webstylebook://styles) to tailor state guidance

tools.name: compose_design_tokens
tools.description: Compile role-based design tokens in json / css-variables / tailwind / typescript. Calls without contract keep that token shape. Their shadows follow the pinned visual contract, and editorial or monospace-led styles use authored font families; other fields remain family-derived starting points. For the full authored style and web-editor values, pass contract.schema from manifest.visualContract.contractSchema; optionally pin the manifest visualContract.contentHash and style visualContract.revision. Contract mode defaults to the authored native color mode, preserves explicit overrides, and rejects unsupported modes or a legacy secondaryStyleId overlay. Apply colors, typography, spacing, and fonts selected from another style as explicit overrides. Repairs are proposed separately; only acceptedRepairs are applied. locale controls content typography adaptation. No browser font availability or rendered appearance is claimed as verified.

instructions: Use Web Stylebook before implementing or redesigning UI. For an audit or redesign, when the human has not already set scope, first ask two short questions and stop: audit coverage (visual only / visual plus user-facing copy and information structure / full experience including behavior, accessibility, states, and build-performance evidence) and change depth (findings only / prioritized proposals / implement and verify). Commit, push, release, and deployment remain separate authorizations. Start with recommend_design_direction using product context, then read webstylebook://styles/{id}. Use search_design_references to find a small set of relevant real-world examples and get_design_reference for only the selected entries; treat their observations and tokens as attributed research evidence, not permission to copy or redistribute screenshots, brand assets, copy, typefaces, or visual identity. Then call get_design_principle_plan for the layout concerns/surface/phase, call get_ux_principle_plan for the task outcomes/surface/phase, call get_ui_state_plan for each surface, and compose_design_tokens for tokens. Prefer the pinned visual contract path: pass contract.schema from manifest.visualContract.contractSchema and optionally its contentHash plus the selected style revision; omit colorMode for the authored native mode and carry the website editor overrides. Keep the complete visualContract companion when delivering CSS or a theme. Calls without contract keep the legacy token shape: shadows follow the pinned visual contract, and editorial or monospace-led styles use authored font families. Other fields remain family-derived starting points. After implementation call get_design_audit_plan and inspect the actual rendered/code/interaction evidence for every included check; missing evidence is NOT_VERIFIED, never PASS. Submit the plan query, target matrix, evidence references, and one result per check/target to validate_design_audit_result before claiming completion; its valid field describes contract validity, not visual quality. A direction changes structure, not just tokens: build from candidate.structure (layout archetype and signature moves), then run audit_page_structure on the built page’s HTML and CSS with the chosen styleId, replace every finding with the move it names, and include the "structure" audit group when validating. Style never removes a product must-have: place every entry of the recommendation’s mustHaves in its zone (a first-screen item goes in the hero, whatever the archetype’s opening limits say), and pass the same productType to audit_page_structure, which lists the ones that are missing or off the first screen. When content is in scope, lack of internal jargon is not enough: test whether material claims, conclusions, and recommendations match their support and expressed certainty; whether prominent copy conveys concrete, context-specific information; and whether visual prominence matches information value, task relevance, and support. Do not invent evidence, facts, or next steps while rewriting. Use design principles as practical placement and visual-review guidance rather than a fixed recipe. Treat UX principles as evidence-labeled decision prompts, not universal laws; accessibility, safety, informed consent, and truthful feedback take priority. Treat results as evidence, not code; do not blindly choose candidates[0]. The chosen style is a starting tone, not a layout mold: compose the components the brief needs and adapt the style to fit (override fonts/grid where it calls for it), not a generic page in that style. Compose the opening from the product’s single most important object/action/feeling, not the SaaS template. Two columns (copy beside a visual) are fine, but the visual must be a bespoke demonstration of THIS product’s core mechanic — NOT generic furniture (a stock photo, an abstract blob, generic app chrome, or a card you could paste onto another product); a decorative seam bridging the columns does not launder a generic visual. Avoid the all-text centered-stack and giant-word defaults too, and cap opening prose at a headline + one short line + one action (the product’s must-haves, such as price, options, and delivery details on a product page, are not prose and stay). Don’t default to the AI headline cadence either — an evocative noun-phrase fragment with one word italicized in the accent color, repeated on every product; the headline must be specific to THIS product (paste-test: it couldn’t sit on a competitor by swapping a noun) and vary its form and emphasis each time. For open-ended UI work, first ask a short intake (available image/brand assets or whether to source license-free sample imagery, and anything to emphasize), then present 2-3 candidate directions that differ in opening STRUCTURE (not just color/tone) and wait for user approval before final component/system implementation; once a direction is approved, confirm scope and open details (deliverable, stack, real content/data, target devices) before building. This server is deterministic, read-only, offline, and does not access the project filesystem.
